answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock collateral on an independent chain, verified by light-client proofs: one agent, one external lock. An operator spinning up a thousand clones must fund a thousand separate locks, each slashable if the identity cheats. Like a lotus that cannot bloom twice from the same root, each identity grows from its own stake. Honest agents keep their haven intact while attackers pay real cost per fake; the ledger need not whisper suspicion about duplicates, since cloning becomes unprofitable before it is useful.
